newsitem.title: DUBAI: PRESS DIGEST - United Arab Emirates - Jan 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - United Arab Emirates - Jan 26.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the United Arab Emirates press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Dubai has registered the heaviest rains in 28 years and wet weather is set to continue.

- The Gulf Aircraft Maintenance Co (GAMCO) has beaten off the competition from a leading British aircraft maintenance company and won a contract to service nine support aircraft of the British Royal Air Force, GAMCO sources said.

- Arab states slashed their actual budget deficits for 1995 by nearly $10 billion as they pressed ahead with reforms and earned more oil income, a report prepared by the Abu Dhabi-based Arab Monetary Fund said.
- Saudi Arabian Airlines and United Airlines of the United States signed an accord to operate joint flights between Jeddah, New York and Los Angeles.
- The number of visitors to Dubai in the year 2000 is expected to be close to three million if past growth rates are maintained, a Dubai visitor survey said.
- German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel left the United Arab Emirates on Saturday after a brief visit to the country lasting several hours.
- The Arab Bank and other regional private investors have created a joint venture with a capital of $60 million to invest in Egypt and more firms could be established, owners said.
- Investments by Gulf Cooperation Council countries in the Gulf aluminium industry rose to $4.3 million. No comparative figure was given.
